# The third triage, and what three tickets now say about an uncalibrated bar

Triage 41 returned the ticket on criterion 2 alone, at 0.52 against the 0.6 bar. Every other criterion is
between 0.67 and 0.85, and criterion 6, the one two review rounds returned the ticket on, is 0.76.

**Criterion 2 was answered 0.83 at triage 30 and 0.52 at triage 41, and the only thing that changed is its
wording.** The second review found it ticked while the delivered rule contradicted its first clause, which was
a fair finding: the wording described the whole-tree rule that record 9 had already amended away. So it was
restated to describe what the code does, naming four refusal sentences and nine fallback reasons. That is a
longer list of claims to evidence, and the answer fell by 0.31. Nothing about the code moved between the two
readings; 1,277 tests pass either way, and the round that closed the reviews' five high findings is recorded at
34 and 35.

**That is now three tickets and the pattern is the finding.** On SEEN-112, criteria 3 and 4 fell from 0.66 and
0.74 to 0.59 and 0.58 when a return reset which checks a tdd record could cite, with no change to the code. On
SEEN-008 the triage passed on the first attempt. Here a criterion made **more accurate** at a reviewer's
request fell from 0.83 to 0.52. In all three cases the bar is `criterion_evidenced = 0.6` at
`harness/thresholds.toml:77`, and the comment above it says what it is: "starting values for SEEN-109 to
calibrate on ten tickets, not numbers anybody has evidence for yet."

So the harness has been enforcing an uncalibrated number as though it were settled, and the three readings that
crossed it were 0.59, 0.58 and 0.52, all within eight hundredths of the bar, none of them caused by a change to
the work. SEEN-109 exists to calibrate this on ten delivered tickets and has not run. That is the decision this
record leaves for the founder rather than working around: the gate is not wrong to ask for evidence, and a bar
nobody has calibrated should not be the thing that decides whether verified work can be delivered.

Recorded and not retried. A fourth reading of the same criterion would be retrying a refused gate, which is
what SEEN-112's criterion 3 forbids and what this session has already done too often.
